overview: White fianchettoes the king's bishop, avoiding the sharp Vienna Gambit and Bc4 lines, and aims for a slow build-up with Bg2, Nge2 and d3. Black usually replies ...Bc5, ...Nf6 and ...d5, striking the centre. The game is calm and manoeuvring with few forced lines.

white_ideas.idea: Play Bg2, Nge2 and d3 or d4, keeping the centre solid.
Use the fianchetto bishop to pressure the long diagonal and f5/d5.

black_ideas.idea: Seize the centre quickly since White's fianchetto is slow.

typical_structures.structure: Open e-file with symmetric pawns and White's fianchetto bishop.

character.notes: Quiet fianchetto set-up; no early forcing play.

gambit.notes: No sacrifice in the main line.

structure.notes: Centre pawns remain with tension on e4/e5.

sublines_that_differ.name: Mariotti Gambit
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nc3 Nc6 3. g3 Bc5 4. Bg2 h5 5. Nf3 h4
sublines_that_differ.how: A rare Black pawn push with kingside play, different in character.

sublines_that_differ.name: Pollock Gambit
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nc3 Nf6 3. g3 Bc5 4. Bg2 Nc6 5. Nge2 d5 6. exd5
sublines_that_differ.how: Gambit via a different move order, sharper play.

character.reason: Quiet fianchetto with no forcing play.

gambit.reason: No sacrifice in the main line.

plans.reason: g3 and Bg2 is the point.
